elements.quote: Cytokine release syndrome with elevated levels of interleukin-6 (IL-6) is associated with multiorgan damage and death in severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). As of October 2020, cumulative moderate-certainty evidence from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) showed that the IL-6 receptor antagonist tocilizumab reduces the risk of mechanical ventilation in hospitalized COVID-19 patients, without affecting short-term mortality [1].
elements.reason: The Introduction describes current knowledge on IL-6, tocilizumab, and remaining uncertainty about mortality effects.

elements.quote: As several RCTs have been published since our initial review, and as per peer reviewers' and editor's recommendations, this update includes observational studies up to January 2021, and future updates will include only data from RCTs.
elements.reason: The need for the updated review is explained by newly published RCTs and the living review design.

elements.quote: This report is the fi rst update of our living systematic review assessing the ef fi - cacy and safety of tocilizumab in COVID-19 patients [1].
elements.reason: This is an update and it explicitly identifies and cites the previous living systematic review (reference [1]).

elements.quote: Cytokine release syndrome with elevated levels of interleukin-6 (IL-6) is associated with multiorgan damage and death in severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19).
elements.reason: The proposed mechanism (IL-6-driven cytokine release syndrome targeted by an IL-6 receptor antagonist) is briefly described.
Tocilizumab is a single-drug intervention, not a complex intervention with multiple components; no logic model requirement applies.

elements.quote: Objectives: Cytokine release syndrome with elevated interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels is associated with multiorgan damage and death in severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). Our objective was to update the data in a living systematic review of the literature concerning the efficacy and toxicity of the IL-6 receptor antagonist tocilizumab in COVID-19 patients.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states the review objective: to update a living systematic review on the efficacy and toxicity of tocilizumab in COVID-19 patients.

elements.quote: The participants were hospitalized COVID-19 patients, and intervention was tocilizumab versus placebo or standard of care.
elements.reason: P, I, and C are clearly stated in the abstract methods (hospitalized COVID-19 patients; tocilizumab vs placebo/standard of care), and outcomes are implied by 'efficacy and toxicity' and the results reported (mortality, mechanical ventilation, composite poor outcome), but the planned outcomes are not fully enumerated within the objective statement itself.

elements.quote: Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies at low or moderate risk of bias. The participants were hospitalized COVID-19 patients, and intervention was tocilizumab versus placebo or standard of care.
elements.reason: The abstract states eligible designs (RCTs; observational studies at low/moderate risk of bias), population (hospitalized COVID-19 patients), intervention and comparator, but a full eligibility criteria section (e.g., settings, follow-up requirements) is not provided in the retrieved Methods text; the paper refers to prior review methodology.

No evidence of eligibility criteria regarding dissemination year, language, or publication status (e.g., preprints were searched but no explicit inclusion/exclusion rules for publication type, language, or date are reported).
The retrieved evidence does not distinguish exclusion of studies because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: Using available data from five studies [2,3,5 e 7], we assessed the effect of steroids on the composite of mortality or mechanical ventilation in patients taking tocilizumab versus controls. The risk ratios for patients receiving steroids and those not receiving steroids were 0.87 (95%CI 0.68 e 1.12) and 0.99 (95% 0.85 e 1.16) respectively.
elements.reason: Synthesis groups (RCTs vs cohort studies; subgroup analyses by steroid use and mechanical ventilation status) and comparisons (tocilizumab vs control) are evident, but a Methods section explicitly specifying and linking groups for each synthesis to the review objectives is not fully described.

elements.quote: As several RCTs have been published since our initial review, and as per peer reviewers' and editor's recommendations, this update includes observational studies up to January 2021, and future updates will include only data from RCTs.
elements.reason: A rationale is given for including observational studies in this update and restricting future updates to RCTs, but no rationale is provided for other restrictions such as limiting observational studies to low or moderate risk of bias.

elements.quote: Using the same methodology and search databases detailed in our previous review [1], we searched for new studies published through 24th February 2021 and updated our analysis using the same quality assessment tools and analytical methods. As several RCTs have been published since our initial review, and as per peer reviewers' and editor's recommendations, this update includes observational studies up to January 2021, and future updates will include only data from RCTs.
elements.reason: The manuscript references the methodology of a previous review for eligibility and synthesis decisions and mentions decisions about which study types (RCTs vs observational) are included in each update/synthesis, but the retrieved evidence does not explicitly describe processes (e.g., tabulating intervention characteristics against planned groups) for deciding which studies entered each specific synthesis/meta-analysis. Table 1 summarizes RCT characteristics, but no explicit decision process per synthesis is reported in the retrieved text.

No methods for preparing data for synthesis are described, such as handling of missing summary statistics or data conversions. The manuscript only states reuse of previous methods ('we searched for new studies... and updated our analysis using the same quality assessment tools and analytical methods', text_6) and reports a post hoc correction for survivor bias in the Results section (text_7) without describing data preparation methods in the Methods section.

elements.quote: Table 1 summarizes the characteristics of eligible RCTs and includes the design, setting, inclusion criteria, disease severity and de fi nition of endpoints.
elements.reason: The content of the main table (Table 1) describing study characteristics is described, but the Methods section does not systematically describe the tabular structures used to display results; it only refers to using 'the same ... analytical methods' from a previous review (text_6).

elements.quote: Fig. 1. (A) Forest plot for the effect of tocilizumab on 28 e 30 days mortality in randomized controlled trials. (B) Forest plot for the effect of tocilizumab on risk for mechanical ventilation in randomized controlled trials. (C) Forest plot for the effect of tocilizumab on 28 e 30 days composite of poor outcome in randomized controlled trials.
elements.reason: Forest plots and a contour-enhanced funnel plot are used and identified in figure captions and Results text (e.g., 'Contour-enhanced funnel plot and Egger's test', Supplementary Material Figs S3-S6), but the Methods section does not explicitly describe the graphical methods; it only defers to the previous review's 'analytical methods' (text_6).

No retrieved evidence states the basis for ordering or grouping studies within the tables or forest plots (e.g., subgrouping of double-blind vs open-label RCTs is shown in figures but no rationale/ordering basis is reported).

elements.quote: Contour-enhanced funnel plot and Egger's test for small-study effects (p 0.27) did not show evidence of publication bias (Supplementary Material Fig. S5).
elements.reason: A non-standard graph (contour-enhanced funnel plot) is used, but no rationale for choosing it is reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
No software package or version used for statistical synthesis is reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
Meta-analysis was performed (pooled RRs reported), so no alternative synthesis method needed to be described.

elements.quote: We pooled crude risk ratios (RRs) of RCTs with a random effects model and evaluated inconsistency between studies with I 2 .
elements.reason: A random-effects model is reported, but no rationale for choosing this model is provided.

elements.quote: Risk Ratio - Weight M-H, Random, 95% Cl
elements.reason: Forest plot tables and figures (e.g., table_1, table_2, figure_3) show the Mantel-Haenszel random-effects method was used for pooling risk ratios.

elements.quote: evaluated inconsistency between studies with I 2
elements.reason: I-squared is explicitly reported as the method to assess heterogeneity, and I2 values are given for each meta-analysis.

elements.quote: Heterogeneity: Taua = 0.05; Chia= 3.43, df= 2 (P = 0.18); P= 42%
elements.reason: Tau-squared values are reported in the forest plots, but the between-study variance estimator (e.g., DerSimonian-Laird) is not named.
The method used to calculate confidence intervals for the random-effects summary effect is not reported.
No other random-effects implementation details (e.g., continuity corrections, weighting specifics beyond M-H) are described in the retrieved evidence.
No Bayesian meta-analysis was performed; frequentist (Mantel-Haenszel random-effects) methods were used.
No methods for handling statistical dependency among multiple estimates from the same study are described.
No planned syntheses judged impossible or inappropriate, with reasons, are reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: We also contacted all fi rst authors of eligible RCTs for additional data for subgroup analyses.
elements.reason: Subgroup analyses were performed (e.g., by blinding status, steroid use, mechanical ventilation) but the Methods section does not explicitly describe the methods used to explore causes of heterogeneity; the review states it reused 'the same quality assessment tools and analytical methods' from a prior review.

elements.quote: The risk ratios for patients receiving steroids and those not receiving steroids were 0.87 (95%CI 0.68 e 1.12) and 0.99 (95% 0.85 e 1.16) respectively.
elements.reason: Factors and levels are reported (steroid use yes/no, mechanical ventilation yes/no, double-blind vs open-label RCTs), but the expected direction of effect modification is not stated.
The evidence does not explicitly state whether analyses used study-level variables, within-study contrasts, or both; subgroups appear study-level but this is not reported as such.

elements.quote: Test for suboroup differences: Ch*= 1.03, df= 1 (P = 0.31), a= 3.1%
elements.reason: Forest plots report a formal chi-squared test for subgroup differences, indicating the method used to compare subgroup effects.
Meta-analysis was conducted for all outcomes; no narrative/synthesis-without-meta-analysis approach is reported, so informal heterogeneity exploration methods do not apply.
The manuscript does not identify which heterogeneity analyses were pre-specified versus post hoc.

elements.quote: To study the potential effect of survivor bias on the observed results, we multiplied the RR ... of studies that did not adjust for survivor bias and their corresponding 95%CIs by 1.6 and pooled the new adjusted effect estimates. The corrected pooled adjusted RR for mortality from the 28 cohorts was 0.69 (95%CI 0.53 e 0.89, I 2 83%)
elements.reason: The manuscript reports an exploratory re-analysis addressing survivor bias (correcting RRs by a factor of 1.6), which functions as a sensitivity analysis, but no analyses are explicitly labelled or described as sensitivity analyses in the Methods; only this one analysis is reported, without full methodological detail.
No statement identifies any sensitivity (or post hoc) analysis as pre-specified or not pre-specified; the survivor-bias correction appears post hoc but is not identified as such.

elements.quote: Contour-enhanced funnel plot and Egger's test for small-study effects (p 0.27) did not show evidence of publication bias (Supplementary Material Fig. S5).
elements.reason: Reporting/publication bias assessment is reported (funnel plot, Egger's test) but only in the Results; the Methods section merely states 'the same quality assessment tools and analytical methods' from a previous review without describing the reporting-bias assessment methods.
No reporting-bias assessment tool with domains/items or process for deriving an overall judgement is described in the retrieved evidence.
No adaptations to an existing reporting-bias tool are described.
No newly developed reporting-bias tool is reported.
The number of reviewers, their independence, and disagreement-resolution procedures for reporting-bias assessment are not reported in the retrieved evidence.

Although authors were contacted ('We also contacted all first authors of eligible RCTs for additional data for subgroup analyses'), this was for subgroup data, not for obtaining or confirming information related to missing results/reporting bias.
No automation tools for reporting-bias assessment are described.

elements.quote: We assessed the certainty of evidence using the GRADE approach.
elements.reason: The GRADE tool is named, though no version is specified; the tool itself is clearly stated.
